setup: The total differential adds up the first-order effect of each variable: \(dz = z_{x}\,dx + z_{y}\,dy\).

steps.say: Put the two into \(dz = z_{x}\,dx + z_{y}\,dy\): \(dz = ([[zx]])\,dx + ([[zy]])\,dy\).
At the starting point \(([[p]], [[q]])\) they are \(f_{x} = [[gx]]\) and \(f_{y} = [[gy]]\).
The moves are \(dx = [[dx]]\) and \(dy = [[dy]]\), so \(df = [[gx_p]] \cdot [[dx_p]] + [[gy_p]] \cdot [[dy_p]] = [[est]]\): the linear estimate of the change, not the exact change.
So \(dQ = Q_{K}\,dK + Q_{L}\,dL = [[qk]] \cdot [[dk_p]] + [[ql]] \cdot [[dl_p]] = [[dq]]\): the linear estimate of the change in output.
